dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you've been having a fever after your delivery — can you tell me how many days ago you gave birth, and when the fever started?
I gave birth about three days ago, and the fever started yesterday. I've been feeling pretty uncomfortable since then.
Thank you. Was your delivery vaginal or by cesarean section, and were there any complications like prolonged labor or prolonged rupture of membranes?
It was a vaginal delivery, and yes, my labor was quite long – it took a really long time before my baby finally came. My son was pretty big too, 11 pounds!
Have you noticed any foul-smelling or unusual vaginal discharge since the delivery, and is the lochia heavier than expected?
I haven't really noticed any bad smell, but I'm not sure what's normal for the discharge. It doesn't seem heavier than I expected, but my belly has been really tender and sore.
Can you show me where exactly your belly is tender — is it low down in the middle, over your uterus, or more to one side? And are you having any pain or burning when you urinate?
It's low down in the middle, right over where I think my uterus is. No, I don't have any burning when I urinate, but I have been going to the bathroom a lot more often than usual.
Are you experiencing any chills, body aches, or feeling generally unwell? And how are your breasts — any redness, engorgement, or tenderness that could suggest a breast infection?

I have had some chills along with the fever, and I do feel pretty run down overall. My breasts are a bit engorged since my milk came in, but they're not red or anything, just the normal fullness from breastfeeding.

Given your fever, chills, and uterine tenderness after a prolonged labor, I'm concerned about an infection of the uterine lining. Let me check your vital signs and run some blood work.
